A distributed ledger differs from a traditional ledger in that no single party to the transaction controls it. All entries are made simultaneously in each copy of the ledger, and each entry must be agreed to by all of the members who share it. Each transaction in the ledger is referred to as a “block.” which is added chronologically to prior blocks, forming a “blockchain™ of recorded transactions. The result is a highly secure record of business transactions with an audit trail that is permanent and “tamper proof.” ‘While blockchain was originally developed as the accounting platform for the cryptocurrency Bitcoin, it is now seeing wide use in a variety of business settings. Walmart currently uses block- chain technology to track 1.1 million items from the manufacturer to its store shelves.
